issues.message: The roof does not reach past the walls on any two opposite sides: give it one block of overhang.

notes.detail: Chest, grindstone, barrel, log pile, chopping block and composter, but the plot is six bare raised dirt strips and the gate and piers carry nothing.
notes.purpose: Without saplings (decoration step only) the plot reads as empty garden beds; two small oaks are the only sign of a tree plantation.
notes.roof: Automatic 'no overhang' warning is a false alarm: the shed roof has one block of overhang all round (stairs at z=6 and z=10, gable ends at x=2 and x=8), 45 degrees, slab ridge, two-tone.
notes.scale: Young oaks are 3-high trunks with a 3x3 blob: ok as young trees, but the shed is a 3 x 1 alcove.

visual.summary: An 11 x 11 fenced plot with a coarse dirt path, six raised dirt planting strips, two young oaks, a gateway beam and a small open dark-oak shed with log pile and woodpile at the back.
problems: Planting strips (z=1,3,5) render as bare dirt in L1: put at least a few saplings or seedlings (or a row marker/fence edging) in L1 itself so the plot reads as a tree nursery, not empty garden beds.

Leaves of the two young oaks run into the shed eave: leaf at (8,5,6) sits on the roof stair and leaves at (2,3,6)/(8,3,6) press against the shed posts, so from the front the canopies swallow the shed; trim them back so the eave at z=6 is clear.

Shed interior is a 3 x 1 alcove (x4..6, z8) holding chest, grindstone and barrel in a row: reads as a stall more than a woodcutter's shed; give it a real working depth (2 deep) or turn it into an open-fronted lean-to with a bench.
Corner piers (0,0..1,0), (10,0..1,0), (0,0..1,10), (10,0..1,10) are bare 2-high cobblestone stubs: cap them (slab or wall) so they read as finished posts.

Reach: the shed floor, workstation (chest, grindstone, barrel), yard and every planting row are reached; the unreached places are roof slopes, leaf tops, pier tops and the gateway roof, which is fine.

issues.message: No door on the front half (z = 0 is the front, toward the easel).
The roof does not reach past the walls on any two opposite sides: give it one block of overhang.

notes.purpose: From the outside it reads as a fenced plot with a woodcutter's shed and a log yard. But the planting beds are filled with permanent 'young trees' (an oak log with persistent leaves on top), which Carlton asked to keep clear for saplings to grow.
notes.roof: False alarm on the roof warning: the shed's roof overhangs 1 block on both eave sides (dark oak stairs at x0 and x6) and at both gable ends (z5, z10).
notes.scale: The 2-tall log+leaf 'young trees' read as hedges or bushes, not trees.
notes.detail: The shed is good (2-deep inside with chest, grindstone and barrel, windows, door). The plot is bare apart from the fake trees and a composter.
notes.artefacts: Ignores Carlton's v1 note: the sapling spots must be clear and decoration moved outside the plot. The beds still hold fake young trees (log + leaves), and props stand inside the plot. No floating blocks. Layer 0 stands on the grass (groundLayer -1), so the dirt beds and the coarse-dirt path are raised 1 block; the path block (5,0,0) shows as a lump in the gateway.

visual.summary: Level 1: an 11 x 11 spruce-fenced plantation on capped cobblestone piers, with a dark oak gateway, raised dirt beds of young trees either side of a coarse-dirt path, a 5 x 4 gabled woodcutter's shed (chest, grindstone, barrel) and a log pile at the back.
problems: Ignores Carlton's v1 note: the sapling spots must be clear and decoration moved outside the plot. The beds still hold fake young trees (log + leaves), and props stand inside the plot.

Carlton's v1 note (all levels) is not met: sapling spots must stay clear, and decoration belongs outside the planting area. The L1 beds at z1 and z3 (x1..3 and x7..9) are filled with log+leaf props: oak logs at (1,1,1), (3,1,1), (7,1,1), (9,1,1) and the same at z3, a leaf at (2,1,z)/(8,1,z) between them, and leaf heads at y2. Leave the beds as bare dirt (or real saplings), so soldiers can plant and the trees can grow.
Decoration inside the plot: the composter (9,0,5) and the chopping block (1,0,5) stand at the head of the tree rows. Move them to the log yard or outside the fence.
Last round fixed: the corner piers are capped (cobblestone walls), the big oaks are gone from the shed eave, and the shed is now 2 deep inside.
Reachability: fine. The shed floor and workstation, the yard, the path and all beds are reached; unreached are only roof slopes, leaf tops and the gateway top.
